key_terms.meaning: A pixel whose 3×3 neighbourhood differs from it in every direction; the mask with centre 8 and all other weights −1 gives a large response only there.
A 3×3 mask tuned to one direction, such as two rows of 1s and one row of −1s, gives its largest response on a thin line of that direction.
The vector (G_x, G_y) of first derivatives; its magnitude √(G_x²+G_y²) is large where brightness changes fast.
Detects edges as zero crossings of the Laplacian of a Gaussian-smoothed image, giving closed thin boundaries.
Finds edges by Gaussian smoothing, gradient, non-maximum suppression and hysteresis, aiming for good detection and one-pixel width.
Keeps a gradient pixel only if its magnitude is larger than the two neighbours along the gradient direction.
Joins nearby edge pixels or fragments that agree in position and direction into longer boundaries.
Each edge pixel votes for all parameter values of a shape through it; peaks in the accumulator are detected shapes.
One grey level T splits the whole image into object and background: g(x,y)=1 if f(x,y)>T, else 0.
Chooses T that maximises the between-class variance σ_B²(T)=ω₀ω₁(μ₀−μ₁)², where ω are class fractions and μ class means.
A seed is a starting pixel or region; the predicate is the test, such as |f−seed mean|≤τ, that decides whether a neighbour joins.
Recursively split a region when its predicate fails, then merge adjacent regions that satisfy a similarity predicate.
The set of pixels that drain to one local minimum in the grey-level landscape under flooding.
The ridge separating two catchment basins; it becomes the boundary between segmented regions.
A closed curve that moves to minimise internal bending energy plus image energy so it settles on object boundaries.
E = ∫ [α|v′(s)|² + β|v″(s)|² + E_image(v(s))] ds; α and β control stretch and bending, E_image attracts to edges.
A boundary written as a string of direction numbers, such as 0 to 7 for 8-neighbour steps, from a chosen start.
A number or vector computed from a boundary, such as perimeter, compactness or Fourier coefficients, used for matching.
E = C − H, where C is the number of connected components and H the number of holes in a region.
A summary of grey-level arrangement, such as contrast, energy or entropy from a co-occurrence matrix, not just mean brightness.

takeaways: A 3×3 mask response separates an isolated point, a thin line and an edge because each has a different local pattern.
Edge detectors respond to derivatives; Marr-Hildreth uses second-derivative zero crossings and Canny uses gradient plus thinning and hysteresis.
Raw edges are fragments; edge linking and the Hough transform build boundaries locally or by global voting.
Global thresholding works when object and background grey levels are well separated, and Otsu picks the cut by maximising between-class variance.
Region growing, splitting and merging replace one grey-level cut with local similarity tests and produce closed regions.
Watershed segmentation floods the grey-level landscape and places boundaries where basins meet.
An active contour balances smoothness against image attraction, so it can close a boundary across small edge gaps.
Chain codes turn a boundary into a compact string, and normalisation makes it independent of start point and rotation.
Region descriptors such as area, Euler number and texture summaries let a vision system compare objects without storing every pixel.
bank_note: Long answers usually stress the full segmentation pipeline — detector or threshold rule, region or boundary construction, and a descriptor with a small worked example.

bank.q: Explain point, line and edge detection using 3×3 masks. State the response formula and give one mask for each.
outline: Point mask with centre 8 and all other weights −1
Line masks for horizontal, vertical and diagonal thin lines
Edge masks approximate a first derivative
Response R = sum of mask weights times pixel values
Threshold each response to mark detections

bank.q: Compare gradient operators with the Marr-Hildreth and Canny edge detectors. Which steps make Canny give thin, connected edges?
outline: Gradient gives magnitude and direction from first derivatives
Sobel and Prewitt use 3×3 derivative masks
Marr-Hildreth smooths with Gaussian then finds Laplacian zero crossings
Canny adds non-maximum suppression and hysteresis
Canny aims for good detection, good localisation and one-pixel width

bank.q: Explain global thresholding and Otsu's method. Define between-class variance and show how the best threshold is chosen.
outline: Threshold T maps pixels to object or background
Histogram should be bimodal for a clean cut
Otsu tries every T and computes class fractions and means
Between-class variance σ_B²=ω₀ω₁(μ₀−μ₁)²
Choose T with maximum σ_B²

bank.q: Explain chain codes and boundary descriptors. How is a chain code made independent of start point and rotation?
outline: 8-neighbour chain code uses direction numbers 0 to 7
Start point changes the string
Rotation changes every direction number by a constant
Normalise start by choosing a canonical rotation
Descriptors such as perimeter or Fourier coefficients summarise shape

bank.q: For a small image with a given histogram, compute the Otsu threshold step by step. Show class fractions, class means and between-class variance for two candidate thresholds.
outline: Build or read the histogram
For each candidate T, compute ω₀, ω₁
Compute μ₀, μ₁ and σ_B²
Compare σ_B² values
Select the T with the largest value and apply it

bank.q: Three edge points lie on a line. Show their votes in a Hough accumulator for two chosen θ values and explain how the peak gives the line.
outline: Line equation ρ = x cosθ + y sinθ
Each point votes for many (ρ,θ) pairs
For a fixed θ compute ρ for each point
Accumulator bin counts votes
Peak bin gives the line parameters

bank.q: Draw the split-and-merge steps for an 8×8 image containing two bright squares on a dark background. State the predicate used at each step.
outline: Split a quadrant when its pixels are not uniform
Use a predicate such as grey-level range ≤ τ
Stop splitting homogeneous quadrants
Merge adjacent regions with similar mean grey level
Final regions should match the two squares

bank.q: Flood a 1-D grey-level profile with two minima. Mark the catchment basins, the watershed line and the final regions.
outline: Treat grey level as height
Water rises from each local minimum
Each minimum collects a catchment basin
Basins meet at a ridge
The ridge is the watershed line

bank.q: Compare edge-based, threshold-based and region-based segmentation for an image with uneven illumination. Which method would you choose and why?
outline: Edge methods can break under low contrast
Global threshold fails when illumination shifts grey levels
Region growing uses local similarity but needs good seeds
Preprocessing or local thresholding may be needed
Justify choice with expected failure modes

bank.q: Discuss how Gaussian sigma, low hysteresis threshold and high hysteresis threshold change a Canny edge map. Relate each parameter to broken edges and false edges.
outline: Larger sigma smooths noise but shifts edges
Small sigma keeps noise and false edges
Low threshold keeps weak edges and noise
High threshold removes weak but real edge parts
Hysteresis connects weak pixels to strong ones

bank.q: Explain the internal and image terms of an active contour. Why do initialization and parameter values matter, and what happens at boundary gaps?
outline: Internal energy controls stretching and bending
Image energy attracts curve to edges
α and β set smoothness
Initialization affects which boundary is found
Curve can bridge small gaps but may leak through large ones

bank.q: Design a segmentation and representation pipeline to count holes in metal parts on a conveyor. Use thresholding, morphology, watershed if needed, chain codes and the Euler number.
outline: Preprocess and choose threshold or Otsu
Clean mask with morphology
Separate touching parts with watershed if needed
Find boundaries and chain-code them
Use Euler number E=C−H to count holes
State validation and failure cases

glossary.def: Partitioning an image into non-overlapping regions that have similar properties.
A boundary between regions where brightness changes rapidly.
The quantity √(G_x²+G_y²), where G_x and G_y are first derivatives.
The second-derivative operator ∇²f = ∂²f/∂x² + ∂²f/∂y².
A sign change in a second-derivative response, often used as an edge location.
A detector that smooths with a Gaussian and then applies the Laplacian.
A thinning step that keeps only local maxima along the gradient direction.
A rule that keeps strong edge pixels and weak pixels connected to them.
The space of shape parameters in which edge pixels cast votes.
An array of bins that counts votes in the Hough transform.
A grey level T used to divide pixels into classes.
A histogram with two peaks, one for object and one for background.
The threshold that maximises between-class variance.
Starting from seeds and adding neighbouring pixels that satisfy a similarity predicate.
A rule that decides whether a pixel or region joins another region.
A recursive splitting of an image into four quadrants at each step.
Segmentation by flooding the grey-level landscape and finding where basins meet.
A seed imposed in marker-controlled watershed segmentation.
A deformable closed curve that minimises an energy to fit object boundaries.
A string of direction numbers that traces a boundary step by step.
A chain code rotated to a canonical start, often the smallest integer form.
The number of connected components minus the number of holes.
The arrangement of grey levels over a region, beyond simple mean brightness.
A matrix counting pairs of grey levels at a fixed offset.
